evidence.V1: Silhouette reads as a picket fence from front and three-quarter (pointed picket tips, two rails, capped post); top view is thin but that is inherent to a fence run.
evidence.V2: Clear hierarchy: dark capped post (big), rails and pickets (medium), chamfered post cap and ink nails (small).
evidence.V3: Confident stylised picket proportions with slight height variation between pickets; capped post anchors the run; nothing floats (touches_floor true).
evidence.V4: Consistent small chamfers on pickets, rails, post and cap catch the light in the rails/post close-ups.
evidence.V5: Close-ups clean: no pinches, seams or z-fighting on pickets, rail ends or post cap.
evidence.V6: Oak in two values (pale pickets/rails, dark post) plus ink nails; colourways stay disciplined.
evidence.V8: Single LF_VertexColor material, smooth shading, chamfered edges, ink iron nails: matches the kit wood treatment.
evidence.V9: Studio line: Anchored, CollisionFidelity Box, CanTouch off, Color white, SmoothPlastic, grid-corner pivot; T1 tiling pass.

top_fixes: Nails appear on only three pickets; put a nail pair on every picket (or none) so the small detail reads as deliberate
Run ends without a post on the open rail end; consider an optional end-post variant for the last segment
Add a touch more irregularity to picket tips/tilt to push the stylisation
